record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Can one prove the existence of a limiting regime in which solutions of the Einstein equations reduce to Newtonian spacetimes?

evidence.quote: Prove the existence of a limit in which solutions of the Einstein equations reduce to Newtonian spacetimes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein field equations of general relativity for a Lorentzian spacetime $(M,g)$ coupled to a matter model (for instance a perfect fluid). Introduce a dimensionless parameter $\lambda = 1/c$, where $c$ denotes the speed of light, and consider one-parameter families of solutions $(M, g_\lambda, T_\lambda)$ of the Einstein equations indexed by $\lambda \in (0, \lambda_0]$.

A Newtonian spacetime is a four-dimensional manifold equipped with the Newton–Cartan structure: a closed one-form $dt$ (absolute time), a symmetric positive semidefinite contravariant tensor $h^{ab}$ of rank three with $h^{ab}(dt)_b = 0$ (spatial metric), and a torsion-free connection $\nabla$ compatible with $dt$ and $h^{ab}$, whose Ricci tensor satisfies the Newton–Cartan field equation $R_{ab} = 4\pi G \rho\, (dt)_a (dt)_b$, where $\rho$ is the mass density of the matter source.

Problem. Prove that there exist non-trivial one-parameter families of solutions $(g_\lambda, T_\lambda)$ of the Einstein equations, defined on a common spacetime region, such that as $\lambda \to 0$ the geometric data $(g_\lambda, T_\lambda)$ converge (in a suitable function-space sense, on appropriate space-time domains and for general physically reasonable matter models and initial data) to a solution of the Newton–Cartan equations describing a Newtonian spacetime. In particular, establish a rigorous limiting regime — including, where possible, global-in-time control and treatment of cosmologically relevant settings — in which solutions of the Einstein equations reduce to Newtonian spacetimes.
artifact.status_search_result: Rigorous results on the Newtonian limit of the Einstein equations have been obtained (e.g., Ehlers' frame theory and subsequent work by Rendall, Oliynyk and others using PDE methods with multiple time scales), proving that one-parameter families of solutions to Einstein's equations converge on finite time intervals to Newtonian solutions for various matter models. However, a fully general result covering all physically relevant settings (including global-in-time and cosmological regimes with general matter) is not established, so the problem is regarded as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Editorial note to: On the Newtonian limit of Einstein's theory of gravitation (by Jürgen Ehlers)
status_evidence.snippet: Ehlers' frame theory provides a rigorous framework for the Newtonian limit; subsequent rigorous PDE results have been obtained.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous frameworks and partial results exist for the Newtonian limit.

status_evidence.title: On the Newtonian limit of general relativity
status_evidence.snippet: Given a Newtonian solution there exist one-parameter families of solutions to the full Einstein equations close to the Newtonian solution for finite time.
status_evidence.claim: Partial rigorous results establish the limit on finite time intervals.

status_evidence.title: The Consistent Newtonian Limit of Einstein's Gravity with a Cosmological Constant
status_evidence.snippet: Treats the Newtonian limit including a cosmological constant.
status_evidence.claim: Extensions of the Newtonian limit have been investigated rigorously.
